lines.text: He heard the giant tank groan every night, and told his boss: one day, this thing is going to burst and drown the whole street.
The whole street burst out laughing.
You see, it was the biggest tank in Boston. Fifteen metres tall, and full of nearly nine million litres of sticky molasses.
When it started leaking, the boss had a better idea. He painted the tank brown, so nobody could see the leaks.
And the neighbourhood kids ran over with cups to catch the free syrup.
Then he found a crack running down the side. He showed everyone. Nothing happened.
Then a ship pumped in a fresh load, and one January morning, the air turned warm. The tank groaned louder than ever.
He ran down the street, shouting at everyone to get away from the tank.
Ha! Scared of pancakes, are we?
The workers laughed and sat down for lunch.
Minutes later, rivets shot out like bullets, the tank split open, and a wave of molasses eight metres high roared down the street.
It knocked houses off their foundations and bent the train tracks. Twenty-one people never got out.
Nobody had ever tested the tank. Not even with water. Its steel was too thin for that much weight.
And as the molasses cooled in the winter air, it turned thick as glue, trapping everyone it caught.
The brown paint never stopped a single leak. It only hid the warning.
